findings.title: Migration crashes when embed_category setting has no row
findings.body: The migration dereferences [0]['id'] from the embed_category lookup query without checking whether any row was returned. Site settings are typically only stored when overridden, so many installs will have no embed_category row, or the stored value may not match an existing category name. In that case result[0] is nil and the migration raises NoMethodError, failing the upgrade.

findings.title: Migration imports hosts with unescaped, unnormalized values
findings.body: The migration interpolates the old embeddable_hosts setting values directly into an INSERT statement without SQL escaping, so values containing quotes or SQL can break the migration or execute SQL. It also stores the raw line, including any scheme or path, while EmbeddableHost.record_for_host later compares only uri.host. Migrated values like http://example.com will not match example.com, breaking embedding after migration. Blank lines can also be inserted.

findings.title: create_table uses force: true
findings.body: create_table :embeddable_hosts, force: true will drop an existing table with that name if present. For a new migration this is unnecessary and can silently delete data if the table already exists from a previous migration or plugin. Normal create_table should be used.

findings.title: Host uniqueness is not enforced
findings.body: EmbeddableHost only validates the format of host. There is no uniqueness validation and the migration does not add a unique index. Duplicate host rows can be created, making record_for_host return an arbitrary row and causing unpredictable category assignment and embed-access checks.

findings.title: before_validation crashes when host is nil
findings.body: The before_validation callback calls self.host.sub! without guarding against nil and the model has no presence validation for host. Creating or updating a record without a host, for example via a direct API request, raises NoMethodError instead of returning a validation error.

findings.title: category_id is not validated
findings.body: EmbeddableHost accepts any integer for category_id; there is no existence validation or foreign key constraint. Admin API clients can save dangling category IDs, which will leave host.category nil in the UI and may pass invalid categories to PostCreator during imports.

findings.title: Saved hosts with ports will never match
findings.body: The host validation allows an optional port, and the before_validation callback does not strip it, but record_for_host queries using uri.host, which excludes the port. A record saved as example.com:3000 will not match a request from http://example.com:3000/..., so the host is effectively unusable.

findings.title: update action 500s for unknown id
findings.body: Admin::EmbeddableHostsController#update uses EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first and passes the result to save_host. If the record does not exist, host is nil and save_host calls host.host= on nil, causing a 500 error instead of returning a 404.

findings.title: destroy action 500s for unknown id
findings.body: Admin::EmbeddableHostsController#destroy calls host.destroy on the result of EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first. If no record matches the id, this raises NoMethodError instead of handling the missing record gracefully.

findings.title: Embedded has-many hydration can insert undefined records
findings.body: In _hydrateEmbedded, keys ending in _ids are mapped through _lookupSubType and the result is assigned directly to the pluralized property. If any id cannot be resolved, the array contains undefined. The singular case checks whether the lookup succeeded, but the plural case does not filter missing records, which can cause template or runtime errors.

findings.title: Client may show wrong or blank category after save
findings.body: After saving, the component sets host.category to Discourse.Category.findById(this.get('categoryId')). If categoryId is blank or invalid, the server defaults category_id to the uncategorized category, but the client sets category to nil/undefined, so the displayed category does not match the saved record until reload.

findings.title: Deletion failures are not surfaced
findings.body: destroyRecord is called without a catch handler. If the DELETE request fails, the host remains in the UI and the user receives no error feedback.

findings.title: Embeddable hosts resource defines unimplemented actions
findings.body: resources :embeddable_hosts creates index, show, new and edit routes, but Admin::EmbeddableHostsController only implements create, update and destroy. Requests to the unimplemented routes will error. The route should be restricted to only the implemented actions.

findings.title: PUT /admin/customize/embedding is a no-op
findings.body: Admin::EmbeddingController#update simply re-renders the fetched embedding object and ignores any submitted attributes. If the endpoint is not intended to update anything, it should be removed; otherwise it silently discards changes.
